newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK/Germany seen crucial for RMC, Tarmac.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK/Germany seen crucial for RMC, Tarmac.

text.p: Next week sees another brace of building material company results from RMC Group Plc and Tarmac Plc, with all eyes focused on news about the German and UK markets in particular.

First up is Tarmac on Tuesday. It is expected to return year profits of between 46.5 million and 68 million stg compared with the preceding year's pre-exceptional 97.1 million stg. The dividend is seen remaining flat at 5.5 pence per share.
Tarmac's post-exceptional profit was 20.3 million after taking charges in 1995.
RMC,one of the major firms in the sector reports on Thursday.
Its year profit forecasts range between 248.8 million and 275 million stg compared with 1995's pre-exceptional 329.3 million stg.
That figure excluded a one-off profit of 12.4 million, which bumped profits up to 341.7 million. The dividend is seen at between 26.0 and 27.5 pence per share versus 25.3 pence last year.
Mike Betts, analyst at Goldman Sachs, said he would be interested to see how the revived UK housing market had boosted Tarmac's related divisions as well as an update on the group's cost cutting.
"I will also seeking comfort on the contracting business - the market has heard rumours on problem contracts," added Betts.
UBS said it would be looking for positive news on the UK market as well.
For RMC, once again the crucial angle is what is happening in Germany, which has crippled players across the sector as the economic problems there continue to bite.
Betts said with Germany accounting for 60 percent of RMC's earnings, the market was keen to hear that things were stabilising. Though an upturn is not seen until 1998.
Last month, RMC and other exposed firms were hit by a profit warning from glassmaker Pilkington Plc stemming from continued tough conditions in Germany.
"But Betts said analysts had already build in this factor and the strong stg issue into forecasts. "The days of savage cuts in RMC profit forecasts are hopefully over," he said.
He expects France to remain difficult, but the UK to provide a bright spot in results and a steady performance from U.S. operations.
RMC's shares were up around 2.4 percent or 23-1/2p on Friday at 980p ahead of the results.
